short.title: Ghost existed. The mission couldn't use him.
short.caption: One visible Ghost was only half the job. His mission bindings were missing.

short.title: Preserving Destiny 1
short.caption: Local sign-in, saved characters and the opening mission are partially working.

short.title: The wrong spawn path
short.caption: Increasing the squad count spawned a Ghost without the authored member or performance binding.

short.title: One Ghost. Both bindings.
short.status: Verified after a manual readiness reset
short.caption: The mission now activates the authored member. The automatic rule created exactly one bound Ghost.

short.title: His configured action runs
short.caption: A manual action moved the same Ghost about 21 game units. Automatic timing and torch light remain unverified.

short.title: The Guardian still needs fixing
short.caption: The in-world Guardian is transparent and refractive. A clean inventory preview does not prove this is fixed.

short.title: Next: make the first mission work
short.caption: Resolve progression and torch behavior, then rifle pickup and combat. Mission completion is still open.

short.title: A tested step forward
short.caption: Ghost binding is a real milestone. The full game is still a long-term goal. Follow the next devlog for progress.

long.title: The Ghost was there. His mission bindings weren't.
captions: Today's milestone is a small but useful step in preserving Destiny One: restoring the opening mission's Ghost bindings.
A visible Ghost can look convincing while the mission still has no usable reference to him.
This devlog explains that problem, the tested fix, and what still prevents the first mission from being complete.

long.title: What the local build currently does
captions: The active target is the final PS3 build, version zero one point twenty four, running in RPCS3 with local services.
Recorded tests accept sign-in, restore a saved character, play the revival scenes and hand control to the Guardian.
The Guardian can walk from the highway into the Wall. That is progress, but the Breach still needs reliable mission progression.
These visuals are a montage of actual test captures. They are not a continuous, completed playthrough.

long.title: Why spawning a Ghost wasn't enough
captions: The old mission action increased the desired count in the Ghost squad. The client created a physical Ghost.
Native traces showed that creation path passed no authored member into the actor constructor.
The resulting actor had no member owner or performance owner. The named mission member still had no actor.
So seeing the shell on screen did not prove the mission could address the right Ghost or start his authored action.

long.title: Activate the authored member
captions: The replacement activates the specific authored Ghost member instead of increasing the squad count.
An isolated test created exactly one Ghost and recorded both owner bindings on that same actor.
A second run used the public mission's automatic rule. It repeated the result after the existing manual readiness reset.
The reset is still an external test action. This does not yet establish fully automatic mission progression.

long.title: What the regression checks prove
long.status: 286 checks passed at the binding checkpoint
captions: The binding change passed two hundred and eighty six script and server regression checks.
The new test checks the actual final-build state encoding and prevents a competing count-only Ghost action.
Schema preflight also passed. Those checks establish payload correctness; the live actor observations establish the binding result.
Neither a passing test suite nor a correct payload proves that weapons, combat or the whole mission work.

long.title: A separate movement experiment
captions: With the performance binding present, a separate manual probe used the configured action key found in the game's asset.
The native lookup accepted the key and dispatched the action. The same Ghost moved about twenty one game units.
That narrows the problem: the authored action can run once the correct actor is bound.
Its original timing and completion signal remain unresolved. The experiment is not enabled as an automatic mission cue.
There is also no verified torch beam. A blue Ghost core is not evidence that corridor illumination works.

long.title: Faster repeat tests
captions: After the first viewing, repeat test runs can opt in to skipping the Mars opening cinematic.
The harness checks the exact native prologue stage before sending the skip input.
Successful replay tests still reached the revival scenes and player control. This saves time when testing the same mission repeatedly.

long.title: The rendering fix is still incomplete
captions: The combined graphics changes retain clean setup menus and normal Titan proportions in the inventory preview.
An in-world emote capture exposes a different problem: the Guardian is transparent and refracts the scenery behind him.
A live read found the expected starter armor in the normalized world equipment cache, so the cache is not entirely empty.
That does not identify the rendering cause or prove the armor art loaded correctly. Both gameplay and menu appearance must pass.

long.title: What remains before a playable first mission
captions: The immediate priorities are reliable Breach progression, correct Ghost behavior and a working illumination sequence.
Rifle pickup, combat, mission completion and arrival at the Tower still need implementation and live validation.
Broader destinations, progression systems and multiplayer are longer-term work. There is no claim that the full game is playable.
New backend behavior should preserve a route toward server authority and multiplayer rather than assume one permanent local player.

long.title: A small milestone with useful evidence
captions: The meaningful result today is one Ghost with the authored references the mission needs, plus a verified manual action dispatch.
Code, regression checks and development notes are pushed to the repository. Captures and game data remain private.
The next devlog will follow a tested gameplay improvement. Reports will separate working, experimental and broken behavior.
